Put great fame upon us! Gloss: n̥sméy 'to us'; méǵh₂ 'great'; ḱléwos 'fame'; dʰedʰh₁dʰí 'put (imperative)'.
They drank (it). Gloss: égʷʰent 'they drank'; ógʷʰim 'the (drink/fire, uncertain)'.
The king wanted a son. He asked the goddess (Earth): "Let a son be born to me!" The goddess told the king: "Sacrifice to the heavenly god Dyeus Varuna."
Good fame (fame of goodness). Gloss: wésu 'good'; ḱléwos 'fame (gen.)'.
The sheep, which had no wool, saw horses drawing the heavy wagon, bearing the great load, swiftly carrying the earth.
Let the word go forth for us. Gloss: wékʷos 'word'; nos 'for us'; pró 'forth'; h₁éytu 'let him go'.
Strong mind (a strong-minded spirit). Gloss: ish₁róm 'strong'; ménos 'mind'.
Put imperishable fame upon us! Gloss: ń̥dʰgʷʰitom 'imperishable'; nos 'for us'; ḱléwos 'fame'; dʰedʰh₁dʰí 'put (imperative)'.
"I want a son." "So be it," said the bright sky-god Varuna. Now the king's wife conceived a son.
The king exists; he is childless.
"Hear me, father Varuna!" The voice of the sky-god Varuna came down from heaven to the earth.
Then the sheep, having heard this, enjoyed the field.
The horse said: "Listen, sheep! My heart is grieved: the earth, lord, the sheep's wool, my warm garment... and for the sheep there is no wool."
Let the bone stand; let it stand; let it be shaped/released.
Let them lift up those; let them raise those; and let them set those at their own feet.
